P90 rejects the reading that the beloved is kicked away with the ladder: the lover comes to value him appropriately, and 'valuing appropriately is still valuing'. Alcibiades shows love that does not lead up; the Phaedrus adds a winged soul that regains its wings after three successive philosophical lives.
